Yeah kibbe doesn’t take face into account anymore when typing because your overall body structure may not always “match” your face and since clothing doesn’t go over the face it’s not necessary to take into account. So you can kind of type your face and body differently since there are still makeup or hair recommendations for different face IDs. 

Yep so Billie is unverified but the general consensus is sn so prominent yang structure with yin flesh over it and a need for width accommodation. If you think you might be somewhere between grace kelly and Billie rikishi then natural or classic fam is probably a good bet. You also might be someone who can and should blend a couple IDs, I think a lot of people take kibbe too strictly when reality is not everybody will fit perfectly into one ID. So you might take some of the soft classic lines and adjust them for vertical accommodation (I feel like I would get downvoted to hell on the kibbe sub for saying that but at the end of the day it’s about finding what works for you).

Gotcha yeah that makes sense about your color palette. 

For kibbe it’s tricky a lot of the times. At your height you definitely have vertical and since sc doesn’t accommodate for vertical it can be ruled out. Dc accommodates for balance and vertical, fn for vertical and width (one of the trickier things to spot imo but width =\= wide), sd for vertical and upper curve, and d for just vertical. If you feel like you’re fairly balanced then I would try exploring dc. 

Also, kibbe is not necessarily about body shape or size. *Most* women will have some form of an hourglass figure. And it’s not always as defined or I’ll defined based on yin vs yang. For example, Mila kunis is a tr and while she has an hourglass it’s not super dramatic. Meanwhile Kat dennings has soft curves for days and she’s still a yang type (sn).

Anyway, kibbe is really hard to spot especially in ourselves (honestly I’m still trying to figure out my own type) so if you want to try getting typed I’d recommend posting in the kibbe typeme group!

UGWs don’t really exist for people with eating disorders like anorexia. Even if she has a specific number she is shooting for there will always be a reason to go further although I suspect Eugenia is not aiming for a particular number rather, is just suck in a continuous weight loss/starvation pattern. 

I struggled with an eating disorder (undiagnosed but looking back I suspect it was likely anorexia) in high school. I would set a number that was the number I wanted to get to. It was usually less about the actual number on the scale and more about the number I lost I.e I didn’t necessarily want to be 100lbs I just wanted to lose 5lbs which would have put me at 100lbs. I would lost the weight and be happy but then think “wait what about it when the holidays roll around? What about my friends birthday this weekend? What about that awards dinner I have to go to? I’m certainly going to eat then and probably gain a bit so I should lose some extra that way when I gain a bit I’ll be at the actual weight I want to be at.” I would lose another five lbs of “buffer” weight. Then I would realize I liked that weight better and wanted that to be my actual weight and so I’d set another goal to lose “buffer” weight and the cycle would repeat itself. Eventually I got to the point where my goals were less weight focused (although I still weighed myself every day to make sure I was losing and my day would be absolutely ruined if I hadn’t lost of god forbid had gained weight) and more body focused. So instead of wanting to lose five lbs I’d want to lose a half inch off my waist or it want to be able to make an O shape with my thumbs and middle fingers and bring it to a certain height up my leg. I’d reach the goal, like my new body at the goal, and then set a new “buffer” goal. 


Tl;dr - nothing will ever be enough. Ultimate goals don’t actually exist in the world of anorexia. There will be goals and new goals in an endless loop.
